original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for Pyle disease located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for Pyle disease located?
final_qi.long_answer: Pyle disease (also called metaphyseal dysplasia) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the SFRP4 gene (Secreted Frizzled-Related Protein 4). The SFRP4 gene is mapped to the short arm of chromosome 7, band p14 (7p14.1). Hence, the gene responsible for Pyle disease resides on chromosome 7.

final_answer.long_answer: Pyle disease (metaphyseal dysplasia) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the SFRP4 gene, which encodes secreted frizzled-related protein 4 involved in Wnt signaling and bone remodeling. Molecular mapping places SFRP4 at cytogenetic band 7p14.3 on the short arm of chromosome 7; therefore, the gene responsible for Pyle disease is located on chromosome 7.
